sections.overview: BirdLife treats this Asian jacana as a full migrant across an exceptionally broad range.
sections.identification: In breeding plumage, the male has two elongated central tail feathers; the female is slightly larger.
sections.habitat: It uses freshwater wetlands, including lakes, rice fields and marshes.
sections.diet: It eats aquatic plants, seeds and small invertebrates.
sections.behavior: Long toes help it walk on floating vegetation.
sections.reproduction: Females mate with several males; males incubate eggs and tend chicks.
sections.ecology: Males place nests among emergent plants, often water lilies.
sections.conservation: BirdLife lists the species as globally Least Concern in its 2024 assessment; its population trend is unknown.
